Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 111, verses 1–5:

Explanation of the words:

Tabbat yada Abi Lahab (Tabbat yadā Abī Lahab): i.e., the hands of Abu Lahab ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib have lost, i.e., his deeds have been lost.

Wa tabb (wa tabba): i.e., he himself has lost, for he is among the people of the Fire.

Ma aghna 'anhu malahu (mā aghnā ʿanhu māluhu): i.e., what good did his wealth do him when Allah the Exalted became displeased with him and punished him in this world and the Hereafter.

Wa ma kasab (wa mā kasab): i.e., of wealth, children and other things.

Sayaslā nāran (sayaṣlā nāran): i.e., he will enter a Fire and be scorched by its heat and blaze.

Dhāta lahab (dhāta lahab): i.e., flaming and blazing.

Wa imra'atuhu (wa imra'atuhu): i.e., Umm Jamil al-'Awra'.

Hammalata al-hatab (ḥammālata al-ḥaṭab): i.e., she carries thorns of sa'dan (a prickly plant) and throws them on the path of the Prophet (ﷺ) to harm and annoy him.

Fi jidiha (fī jīdihā): i.e., around her neck.

Habl min masad (ḥablun min masad): i.e., of palm fibre.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he!﴾ These five blessed verses were revealed in response to Abu Lahab, the uncle of the Prophet (ﷺ). It is established that when the verse ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:214] was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) climbed Mount al-Safa and called out: "Wa sabahah! Wa sabahah!" The people gathered around him, and he said to them: "I am a warner to you before a severe punishment. Say: There is no god but Allah, a word by which you will rule the Arabs and by which the non-Arabs will submit to you." Abu Lahab spoke up and said: "Is it for this that you gathered us? May you perish all day long!" Then Allah the Exalted revealed in reply: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾, i.e., Abu Lahab has lost and everything belonging to him has lost. This is a supplicatory sentence, and for this reason he died of a severe illness, so that they could not wash his body; they poured water on him from a distance. As for His saying ﴿and perish he!﴾, it is an announcement from Allah the Exalted of the destruction of 'Abd al-'Uzza, Abu Lahab. His saying ﴿His wealth did not avail him, nor what he earned﴾ means: when Allah became displeased with him and caused him to enter His Fire, his wealth and his children did not avail him, i.e., they did not repel the punishment from him. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿He will enter a Fire of blazing flame﴾ means a fire of intense flaring and kindling. ﴿And his wife﴾, Umm Jamil al-'Awra', ﴿the carrier of firewood﴾, for she used to bring sa'dan thorns and place them on the path of the Prophet (ﷺ) as he went to the dawn prayer at the Masjid al-Haram. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿around her neck is a rope of palm fibre﴾ means: around her neck is a rope of palm fibre, or of the masad of the doum tree. With this, Allah the Exalted has passed judgement on His enemies and the enemies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Guidance from the verses:

1- The declaration of Allah's judgement concerning the destruction of Abu Lahab and the nullification of his plot against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

2- Neither wealth nor children avail a servant anything against the punishment of Allah if he acts in ways that displease Him and abandons what pleases Him.

3- The absolute prohibition of harming the believers.

4- Kinship does not avail anything against shirk and disbelief, for Abu Lahab was the uncle of the Prophet (ﷺ) and he is in the Fire of blazing flame.
